name: Sirius
description: Brightest star in the night sky. Also known as the Dog Star, it is a binary system with a white dwarf companion.

name: Betelgeuse
description: A red supergiant star in Orion, one of the largest stars visible to the naked eye. Notable for its variability and expected to go supernova.

name: Polaris
description: The North Star, a Cepheid variable star used for navigation. It marks the north celestial pole.

name: Vega
description: Fifth brightest star in the sky and part of the Summer Triangle. Used as a photometric standard for calibrating brightness scales.

name: Rigel
description: A blue-white supergiant marking Orion's left foot. One of the most luminous stars in our region of the Milky Way.

name: Antares
description: The heart of the Scorpion. Its name means 'rival of Mars' due to its reddish color. A variable star with a blue companion.

name: Alpheratz
description: The brightest star in Andromeda, also part of the Great Square of Pegasus. A binary star with a mercury-manganese star.

name: Mirach
description: A red giant in Andromeda often used as a guide star to find the Andromeda Galaxy.

name: Almach
description: A multiple star system in Andromeda known for its beautiful color contrast when viewed through a telescope.

name: Altair
description: Part of the Summer Triangle. One of the closest visible stars to Earth, known for its rapid rotation.

name: Tarazed
description: A bright orange giant in Aquila, forming a line with Altair and Alshain.

name: Hamal
description: The brightest star in Aries, an orange giant once used to mark the vernal equinox.

name: Sheratan
description: The second brightest star in Aries, a spectroscopic binary system.

name: Capella
description: Sixth brightest star in the sky. A four-star system with two pairs of binary stars in Auriga.

name: Menkalinan
description: The second brightest star in Auriga, an eclipsing binary star system.

name: Arcturus
description: Fourth brightest star in the night sky. A red giant in BoÃ¶tes, easy to find by following the arc of the Big Dipper's handle.

name: Izar
description: A beautiful double star in BoÃ¶tes, known as Pulcherrima ('most beautiful') for its color contrast.

name: Tarf
description: The brightest star in Cancer, an orange giant with an exoplanet.

name: Cor Caroli
description: The brightest star in Canes Venatici, named 'Heart of Charles' after King Charles I of England.

name: Adhara
description: Second brightest star in Canis Major and one of the brightest ultraviolet sources in the sky.

name: Wezen
description: A yellow-white supergiant in Canis Major, one of the most luminous stars known.

name: Procyon
description: Eighth brightest star in the sky. Part of the Winter Triangle, with a white dwarf companion.

name: Gomeisa
description: The second brightest star in Canis Minor, a hot blue-white star.

name: Deneb Algedi
description: The brightest star in Capricornus, an eclipsing binary system.

name: Canopus
description: Second brightest star in the night sky. A white supergiant used for spacecraft navigation.

name: Miaplacidus
description: Second brightest star in Carina, a blue-white giant star.

name: Schedar
description: The brightest star in Cassiopeia, an orange giant that may be slightly variable.

name: Caph
description: A rapidly rotating giant star in Cassiopeia, part of the distinctive W-shape.

name: Alpha Centauri
description: The closest star system to the Sun. A triple star system including Proxima Centauri.

name: Hadar
description: Also known as Agena, the second brightest star in Centaurus and one of the hottest stars visible to the naked eye.

name: Alderamin
description: The brightest star in Cepheus, will become the pole star around 7500 CE.

name: Diphda
description: The brightest star in Cetus, an orange giant also known as Deneb Kaitos.

name: Menkar
description: A red giant marking the nose of Cetus the sea monster.

name: Mira
description: A famous pulsating variable star, the prototype of Mira variables. Its brightness varies dramatically.

name: Alphecca
description: The brightest star in Corona Borealis, an eclipsing binary also known as Gemma.

name: Gienah
description: The brightest star in Corvus, a blue giant star.

name: Acrux
description: The brightest star in Crux, the Southern Cross. A multiple star system.

name: Mimosa
description: The second brightest star in Crux, a Beta Cephei variable star.

name: Gacrux
description: A red giant in Crux, the closest red giant to the Sun.

name: Deneb
description: Part of the Summer Triangle. One of the most luminous stars known, marking the tail of Cygnus the Swan.

name: Sadr
description: A yellow supergiant at the center of the Northern Cross in Cygnus.

name: Albireo
description: A beautiful double star at the head of Cygnus, famous for its contrasting gold and blue colors.

name: Eltanin
description: The brightest star in Draco, an orange giant in the dragon's head.

name: Thuban
description: An alpha star in Draco, was the pole star during ancient Egyptian times.

name: Achernar
description: The brightest star in Eridanus and ninth brightest in the sky. One of the flattest stars known due to rapid rotation.

name: Pollux
description: The brightest star in Gemini and nearest giant star to the Sun. Has a confirmed exoplanet.

name: Castor
description: A sextuple star system in Gemini, one of the brightest multiple star systems in the sky.

name: Alhena
description: Third brightest star in Gemini, a spectroscopic binary at the foot of the twin Pollux.

name: Alnair
description: The brightest star in Grus the Crane, a hot blue-white star.

name: Kornephoros
description: The brightest star in Hercules, a yellow giant in the hero's shoulder.

name: Rasalgethi
description: A variable red supergiant in Hercules, one of the largest stars known.

name: Alphard
description: The brightest star in Hydra, the Solitary One, an orange giant.

name: Regulus
description: The brightest star in Leo and the heart of the lion. A quadruple star system.

name: Denebola
description: The second brightest star in Leo, marking the lion's tail.

name: Algieba
description: A beautiful double star in Leo's mane, consisting of two orange giants.

name: Arneb
description: The brightest star in Lepus, a white supergiant near Orion.

name: Zubeneschamali
description: The brightest star in Libra, known for its alleged green color, unique among bright stars.

name: Zubenelgenubi
description: A double star in Libra whose name means 'the southern claw', from when Libra was part of Scorpius.

name: Sheliak
description: A famous eclipsing binary in Lyra, prototype of the Beta Lyrae variables.

name: Rasalhague
description: The brightest star in Ophiuchus, marking the head of the serpent bearer.

name: Bellatrix
description: The third brightest star in Orion, marking the hunter's left shoulder. Known as the Amazon Star.

name: Alnilam
description: The middle star of Orion's Belt, one of the most luminous stars visible to the naked eye.

name: Peacock
description: The brightest star in Pavo, a blue star with a unique proper name.

name: Enif
description: The brightest star in Pegasus, an orange supergiant marking the horse's nose.

name: Scheat
description: A red giant in Pegasus, part of the Great Square of Pegasus.

name: Markab
description: Part of the Great Square of Pegasus, a blue giant star.

name: Mirfak
description: The brightest star in Perseus, a yellow supergiant in the Alpha Persei Cluster.

name: Algol
description: The Demon Star, a famous eclipsing binary in Perseus. Known for its regular dimming.

name: Ankaa
description: The brightest star in Phoenix, an orange giant.

name: Fomalhaut
description: One of the brightest stars with a famous debris disk. First star with a directly imaged exoplanet.

name: Naos
description: The brightest star in Puppis, one of the hottest stars visible to the naked eye.

name: Kaus Australis
description: The brightest star in Sagittarius, marking the southern part of the archer's bow.

name: Nunki
description: Second brightest star in Sagittarius, one of the oldest named stars.

name: Shaula
description: Second brightest star in Scorpius, marking the scorpion's stinger.

name: Unukalhai
description: The brightest star in Serpens, marking the serpent's neck.

name: Aldebaran
description: The eye of the Bull in Taurus, an orange giant and one of the brightest stars. Has an exoplanet.

name: Elnath
description: The second brightest star in Taurus, marking the tip of the bull's northern horn.

name: Alcyone
description: The brightest star in the Pleiades cluster, a blue giant in Taurus.

name: Atria
description: The brightest star in Triangulum Australe, the Southern Triangle.

name: Alioth
description: The brightest star in Ursa Major and part of the Big Dipper's handle.

name: Dubhe
description: One of the pointer stars in the Big Dipper, used to find Polaris.

name: Alkaid
description: The end star of the Big Dipper's handle, a hot blue star.

name: Mizar
description: Famous double star in the Big Dipper, paired with Alcor. A sextuple star system.

name: Kochab
description: Second brightest star in Ursa Minor, was the pole star around 1500 BCE.

name: Spica
description: The brightest star in Virgo, representing the ear of wheat. A close binary system.

name: Porrima
description: A beautiful double star in Virgo with two nearly identical white stars.

name: Sadalsuud
description: The brightest star in Aquarius, a rare yellow supergiant.

name: Sadalmelik
description: Second brightest star in Aquarius, another rare yellow supergiant.

name: Phact
description: The brightest star in Columba the Dove.

name: Rotanev
description: Brightest star in Delphinus. Its name is 'Venator' spelled backwards, after astronomer Nicolaus Venator.

name: Sualocin
description: Second brightest in Delphinus. Named 'Nicolaus' backwards after astronomer Nicolaus Cacciatore.
